memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now then, please swear to me by the Lord that you will show kindness to my family, because I have shown kindness to you. Give me a sure sign that you will spare the lives of my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them — and that you will save us from death." — Josh 2:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Rahab's faith is not only in her words; it moves her to act, and to think of others. Having believed that God has given Israel the land, she draws the logical conclusion: Jericho is doomed. So she pleads not only for herself but for her whole family — father, mother, brothers, sisters, everyone belonging to them.

This is what real faith looks like. It does not save itself and forget everyone else. The moment Rahab grasped her own danger and her only hope, her heart turned to the people she loved. Genuine faith always has a family dimension; when we truly understand salvation, we long for those close to us to be saved too.

Notice also her request for "a sure sign." Rahab wanted something certain to hold on to, a solid pledge she could trust. Faith is not vague wishing; it rests on a reliable promise. She was right to seek assurance, and God, through the spies, would give it.

We have a far greater and surer sign — the cross and resurrection of Jesus, God's guarantee that all who trust Him will be saved from death (Rom 8:32). And like Rahab, when we know that hope, we cannot keep it to ourselves. We plead for our families to be under the same covering of grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your faith move you to pray and plead for your family's salvation?
2. What "sure sign" has God given you to rest your hope upon?
3. Who in your life do you long to see brought under God's grace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for the sure hope I have in Christ. Give me Rahab's heart to plead for my loved ones and long for their salvation. Amen.
